then: Expects a clean scan up to the limit, ErrScanContract above it, no extra receive, and a canceled stream context.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanStream that carries this ID.

title: Each operation is an independent root with its provider children
when: Runs the public entry point with a TLS collector and provider calls inside each operation.
then: Expects eight roots with no parent and no link, eight provider spans under their operation, and distinct trace IDs for each operation.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryExport that carries this ID. Monitor runs a keyed watch on the real telemetry runtime, started with controller.SpanNames and provider.call, with the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the watch, the scan and six reconciles each start one provider.call child span through StartOperation.

title: Timeout and terminal outcomes are classified
when: Runs one key with an action that waits for its 5 ms deadline, and then with an action that returns a terminal error.
then: Expects one timeout with one retry, one failure with no retry, and the action in the last histogram bucket.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryOperations that carries this ID.

title: The snapshot and the exposition carry counts and no private value
when: Scans a private key and two others into a two-slot queue, fails the private key once with a private error, and holds the second action.
then: Expects capacity 2, one active, one queued, one retrying and one waiting key, one failure and one retry, and an exposition with the fixed names and no private text.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryOperations that carries this ID.

title: The first controller starts the provider and the last closes it
when: Starts two controller telemetry owners, attaches a queue to each, closes the first twice, then closes the second.
then: Expects one shared provider, the provider still open after the first close, closed after the last, and no retained ownership.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryOwnership that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: Monitor refuses unsafe addresses and a busy listener before the controller starts
when: Calls Monitor with nine unsafe addresses, an empty address, and the address of a listener that is already open.
then: Expects an error and no callback for each unsafe address and for the busy listener, and a nil collector with the callback's error for the empty address.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryOwnership that carries this ID. The ninth unsafe address has no port.

title: A callback failure emits one service.failed event and keeps its error
when: Runs Monitor with a callback that returns a private error whose text panics on format, returns context.Canceled, panics, or calls runtime.Goexit.
then: Expects exactly one service.failed event for the error, the panic and the Goexit, none for success or cancellation, the same error value or ErrRunAborted, and no private text in the output.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryOwnership that carries this ID. The service events go to the probe runtime's Recorder.

title: A retry delay longer than the action timeout is refused
when: Builds a retry policy whose delay is one millisecond longer than the action timeout, then one whose delay equals the timeout.
then: Expects the first policy refused with an error that names the delay and the timeout before any source opens, and the second accepted.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRetryBudget that carries this ID. The load of the checkpoint counts as the source open.

title: A failed attempt is cancelled and its callback joined before the retry delay starts
when: Runs an action that fails while a callback it started is still running, with a retry delay of one second on a fake clock.
then: Expects the attempt's context cancelled and the callback returned before the fake clock records the start of the delay.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRetryBudget that carries this ID. It uses testing/synctest as the fake clock. The callback of the first attempt records the time its context ends; the second attempt must start one delay or more after that time.

title: No attempt starts when the remaining budget cannot cover the delay and a full action
when: Runs a cycle whose remaining work budget is one millisecond less than the retry delay plus the action timeout, after one failed attempt.
then: Expects no second attempt, the failure stored in the cycle checkpoint, and a second attempt in a run whose budget is exactly the delay plus the timeout.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRetryBudget that carries this ID. It uses testing/synctest as the fake clock. It checks the boundary on both sides.

title: A terminal peer failure cancels the pending retries of a parallel cycle
when: Runs a parallel cycle with two keys: key A fails with a retryable error and waits for its delay, and key B then fails with a terminal error.
then: Expects key A's retry cancelled with no second attempt, the terminal error returned, and both workers joined before the checkpoint save.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRetryBudget that carries this ID. It uses testing/synctest as the fake clock.

title: A later success does not clear a failure already stored in the cycle checkpoint
when: Runs a cycle where item 1 fails and its failure is saved, then item 2 succeeds in the same cycle.
then: Expects the checkpoint after the cycle to still hold item 1's failure, and the next cycle to start from item 1.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRetryBudget that carries this ID. Each pass reads one page of one item, and the checkpoint store refuses a save that breaks ValidateCycleTransition.

title: A failed connection attempt does not delay keys already queued
when: Queues three keys, then makes the watch connection fail once with a reconnect backoff of ten seconds on a fake clock.
then: Expects the three queued keys to reach their action before the fake clock advances, and the reconnect to wait its backoff.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueBackoff that carries this ID. The watch queues three keys and its connection then fails with a reconnect delay of ten seconds; the keys must reach their action within one second of the real clock, and no second watch opens. A nested subtest runs a 200 ms action while each watch session fails at once with a 50 ms reconnect delay: the action must finish, and the collector must report a running queue meanwhile. At the end of the delay the runtime takes no new key and lets a running action finish.

title: An interrupted action takes the next capped delay, not a reset delay
when: Fails one key twice to reach its second delay, then interrupts the third attempt by a reconnect.
then: Expects the next delay to be the third step of the capped backoff, not the first step.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueBackoff that carries this ID. It works on the queue with a minimum delay of 1 s, so the third step is 4 s.

title: A successful scan clears the scan backoff
when: Fails two scans in sequence, then lets the third scan succeed, then fails the fourth scan.
then: Expects the delay before the fifth scan to be the first backoff step, not the third.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueBackoff that carries this ID. It works on the scan schedule of the keyed queue.

title: A queued action runs while the next scan waits for its due time
when: Schedules the next scan one minute ahead on a fake clock, then adds one key.
then: Expects the key's action to run without the fake clock advancing.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueBackoff that carries this ID. The next scan is due in one minute; the action must run within one second of the real clock, and no second scan runs.

title: The scan cursor advances only after the item is admitted
when: Fills the queue to capacity, scans a page of two items with the second item blocked at admission, and then cancels the scan.
then: Expects the stored cursor to name the first item, not the second.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueAdmission that carries this ID. ScanFrom emits into the keyed queue through AddWait, with one slot free.

title: The page request context ends before the scan waits for admission
when: Uses a source whose page call records when its context ends, with the queue full when the page returns.
then: Expects the page context ended before the scan starts to wait for admission.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueAdmission that carries this ID.

title: Admission stops on cancellation
when: Blocks a scan at admission with the queue full, then cancels the run context.
then: Expects the scan to return context.Canceled within one second and no item admitted after the cancellation.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueAdmission that carries this ID.

title: Adding a key does not block the caller
when: Fills the keyed queue to capacity and calls Add for one more key from the test goroutine.
then: Expects Add to return without waiting, and the key to be kept as pending or reported as backpressure, never lost.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueueAdmission that carries this ID. Each Add runs under a 100 ms test bound, so a block fails the test.

title: A collector that another running controller holds is refused
when: Starts controller A with a collector, then starts controller B with the same collector while A runs.
then: Expects B refused with an error before it opens a source, and A unaffected.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID.

title: The collector exposes exactly the fixed instrument set
when: Runs a controller with a collector, then gathers the registry.
then: Expects exactly the instruments stego_controller_running, queue capacity, queued, active, retrying, waiting, ready, completed actions by outcome, retries, completed scans, reconnects and one duration histogram, plus stego_controller_cleanup_enabled and the cleanup gauges only when a cleanup source is set, with no other metric name and no label other than outcome.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID. It reads the exposition, with no cleanup source; the bucket bound le of the histogram is part of the histogram. The cleanup gauges of ST-SUP-RP02-LC18 are in the exposition only when a cleanup source is set.

title: The collector size does not grow with the resource count
when: Runs the controller over ten keys and over ten thousand keys, and gathers the series count each time.
then: Expects the same number of series in both runs.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID. It counts the series lines of the exposition.

title: Counters survive a reconnect and gauges reset when the queue stops
when: Completes two actions, forces a watch reconnect, completes one more action, then stops the queue.
then: Expects the completed actions counter to read 3 after the reconnect, and the queued, active, retrying, waiting and ready gauges to read 0 after the stop.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID.

title: A cancelled action schedules no retry in a stopped queue
when: Stops the queue while one action runs, so the action ends cancelled.
then: Expects the retries counter unchanged and no retry entry left in the queue.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID.

title: An interrupted scan does not count as completed
when: Cancels a scan in the middle of its second page.
then: Expects the completed scans counter unchanged.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCollector that carries this ID.

title: The monitor serves only the metrics, with no-store and nosniff
when: Starts Monitor on 127.0.0.1:0 and sends GET to the metrics path, GET to /other and POST to the metrics path.
then: Expects 200 with the Prometheus text content type, Cache-Control no-store and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff for the first, 404 for the second and 405 for the third.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID. A real loopback listener. Monitor does not give the port it binds for port 0, so the test takes a free loopback port first and gives Monitor that address.

title: The monitor registers nothing on the default mux
when: Starts Monitor, then serves a request to http.DefaultServeMux at the metrics path.
then: Expects 404 from the default mux.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID.

title: The monitor binds loopback only
when: Calls Monitor with 0.0.0.0:0, [::]:0 and the address of a non-loopback interface, then with 127.0.0.1:0 and [::1]:0.
then: Expects each of the first three refused with an error and no listener open, and each loopback address accepted with its listener bound to that loopback address only.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID. Monitor does not give the port it binds for port 0, so the test takes a free loopback port first and gives Monitor that address. The test skips the IPv6 case when the host has no ::1.

title: The monitor server has its fixed timeouts and MaxHeaderBytes 4096
when: Starts Monitor, then sends a request with a 9 KiB header, and opens a connection that sends no header.
then: Expects the 9 KiB header answered 431 and the silent connection closed by the server after its header timeout; and expects the read, write and idle timeouts of the server set to nonzero values and the header limit set to 4096 bytes.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID. It reads the server fields through monitorServer.

title: An empty address gives a nil collector and no server
when: Calls Monitor with an empty address and a callback.
then: Expects the callback to receive a nil collector and no listener open on any port.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID.

title: A listener failure stops the controller from starting
when: Calls Monitor with the address of a listener that is already open.
then: Expects an error and the callback never called.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID.

title: When one part exits the monitor closes the listener, cancels the context and joins both
when: Runs Monitor, then makes the callback return an error; in a second run, makes the server fail.
then: Expects in both runs the listener closed, the shared context cancelled, Monitor returning only after both parts return, and the first error returned.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryMonitor that carries this ID. The server fails through a listener whose Accept fails.

title: The telemetry runtime starts before the callback and lives for the callback's whole life
when: Runs Monitor with a callback that starts a nested controller and defers a cleanup that emits a span.
then: Expects the setup span, the nested controller's spans and the deferred cleanup span all exported by one provider with one instance identity.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. The setup and the deferred cleanup each run a standalone ScanFrom, which is its own scan span. The provider set is the OpenTelemetry SDK with exporters in memory, behind the Providers interface that *otel.Runtime satisfies; ST-SUP-Q01 records why the telemetry runtime does not export the controller spans yet. A second subtest starts a telemetry runtime that does not register the controller span names: the start fails with an error that names the missing span name, and the callback never runs.

title: The monitor waits for an ongoing bounded provider close
when: Starts a second Monitor while the first one's provider close blocks for 500 ms.
then: Expects the second runtime to start only after the first close returns.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. It checks the order of the starts and the closes.

title: Each queue registers once and unregisters when its run ends
when: Runs two queues in one monitor, ends one, then gathers the registered queues.
then: Expects one registration per queue while it runs and only the running queue after the other ends.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. It reads the gauge stego.controller.queue.running.

title: A sixty-fifth queue is refused
when: Registers sixty-four queues, then a sixty-fifth.
then: Expects the sixty-fifth refused with an error and the first sixty-four still registered.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID.

title: Cancellation emits no failure event
when: Cancels the monitor context while the callback runs.
then: Expects no failure event in the exported logs.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. The service events go to the probe runtime's Recorder.

title: The callback's value and error identity return unchanged
when: Makes the callback return a sentinel value and a nil error; then makes it return a sentinel error value wrapped once.
then: Expects Monitor to return the same value as the callback in the first run, and in the second run errors.Is with the sentinel to be true and the returned error to be the same value the callback returned.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. It runs with an empty address and with a loopback address.

title: A probe command starts no telemetry
when: Runs the process with the probe command and an OTLP endpoint set to a fake collector.
then: Expects no connection to the fake collector and no provider started.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryStartup that carries this ID. The start function is otel.New; the fake collector is a loopback listener that counts connections. The health endpoint is the real handler of the modes runtime (modes.Readiness.Handler) for the controller mode; a probe of it when the database ping fails exits 1.

title: Each reconcile, scan and watch emits one completion log and one duration sample
when: Runs one reconcile, one scan and one watch session with an in-memory log and metric exporter, at sampling ratio 1 and again at 0.
then: Expects exactly one completion log and one duration sample per operation in both runs, each carrying the operation, the outcome, the retry flag and the span's trace and span IDs, valid also at ratio 0.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryLogs that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A watch span covers one session and ends before the reconnect
when: Runs a watch that disconnects once and reconnects.
then: Expects two watch spans, the first ended before the second starts.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryLogs that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: The completion log severity follows the outcome
when: Runs one action that succeeds, one that is cancelled, one that fails and retries, and one that fails terminally.
then: Expects INFO, INFO, WARN and ERROR in that order.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryLogs that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: Watch start, reconnect and cleanup-summary failure are fixed events
when: Starts a watch, forces one reconnect, and makes one cleanup summary read fail.
then: Expects one log each with the fixed event names of the runtime and no other free-text event.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryLogs that carries this ID. The watch starts again after the reconnect, so the start event can be there twice. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: The controller instruments are the fixed stego.controller.* set with no configurable label
when: Runs a controller and lists the exported instrument names and their attribute keys.
then: Expects every name to start with stego.controller., the list equal to the fixed set, and no attribute key outside the fixed set.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryLogs that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A sweep validates every definition before it starts telemetry
when: Runs a sweep with three definitions, the third invalid, and an OTLP endpoint set to a fake collector.
then: Expects an error naming the third definition, no provider started and no source read.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID. The context carries a telemetry owner with no user, so a start of the provider set is counted; the third definition is a stream with no page function.

title: A sweep with a cancelled context starts no provider
when: Runs a sweep with a context that is already cancelled.
then: Expects nil, as the other entry points of the controller return for a cancelled context, and no provider started.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID. The context carries a telemetry owner with no user, so a start of the provider set is counted. The sweep returns nil, as the code the generator emits does (review of PR 149).

title: A sweep registers no keyed queue
when: Runs a sweep inside a monitor and lists the registered queues.
then: Expects no queue registered.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID. It reads the gauge stego.controller.queue.running while the sweep action runs. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A pass deadline counts as a retry only while the run is active and the error is not terminal
when: Makes a pass exceed its deadline while the run is active, then after the run is cancelled, then with a terminal error.
then: Expects a retry in the first case only.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID. It reads the retry flag of the completion log of the first reconcile. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A page callback that returns no error after its deadline is a timeout, not a source error
when: Makes the page callback return nil one millisecond after its deadline, with a terminal policy on source errors.
then: Expects the page recorded as a timeout and the sweep not stopped by the terminal policy.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID. It reads the outcome of the completion log of the first scan. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: The sweep joins its workers before the next page and before close
when: Runs a sweep whose workers block until released, then cancels.
then: Expects no read of the next page while a worker of the current page runs, and the sweep to return only after every worker returns.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanSweep that carries this ID.

title: A resumed scan returns the completed prefix with the error
when: Resumes a scan of five items where the emitter fails on item 4, then one where the source fails on page 2.
then: Expects progress up to item 3 together with the emitter error, and the progress of page 1 together with the source error.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanProgress that carries this ID. The pages hold two items each.

title: A page above the size bound is refused
when: Makes the source return one item more than the page size bound.
then: Expects an error and no item of that page emitted.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanProgress that carries this ID.

title: Each page read is bounded by the operation timeout
when: Makes the source block on one page past the operation timeout.
then: Expects the page read cancelled with a deadline error at the timeout.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanProgress that carries this ID. The page timeout is 30 ms.

title: A scan from the beginning returns the contract error when its page budget cannot cover the source
when: Scans from the beginning with a page budget of two over a source of three pages.
then: Expects the scan contract error and no partial progress returned.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanProgress that carries this ID. Scan returns only the error, so no progress can come back; a budget that covers the source passes.

title: A scan starts no background work
when: Counts goroutines before a scan and after it returns.
then: Expects the same count after the scan, with no goroutine left from the scan.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestScanProgress that carries this ID. It counts only the goroutines whose stack runs code of the package's own files, after a short settle, so the goroutines of other tests do not change the count.

title: Cleanup sampling runs on its own worker under the action timeout and at the resync interval
when: Enables metrics, blocks a scan, and lets the fake clock pass two resync intervals.
then: Expects two cleanup summary reads while the scan is blocked, each with a context deadline equal to the action timeout.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID. It uses testing/synctest as the fake clock.

title: The cleanup worker is joined on shutdown
when: Stops the controller while a cleanup read blocks.
then: Expects the run to return only after the cleanup read returns.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID.

title: With metrics disabled the cleanup summary is never read
when: Runs the controller with metrics disabled for three resync intervals.
then: Expects zero calls of the cleanup summary reader.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID. It uses testing/synctest as the fake clock.

title: A failed read keeps the last values but marks them unavailable, and so does shutdown
when: Reads one good sample, then makes the next read fail; then stops the controller.
then: Expects the gauges to keep the good values with the availability gauge at 0 after the failure, and at 0 after shutdown.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID. It reads the snapshot and the gauge stego_controller_cleanup_available of the exposition.

title: A malformed sample or a terminal access error stops the controller
when: Returns a sample with a count of zero and an oldest time set; in a second run, returns a permission error.
then: Expects the controller to stop with an error in both runs.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID.

title: Any other failed sample is reported and sampled again
when: Returns a transient error from one read, then a good sample.
then: Expects one failure event, the controller still running, and the good sample read at the next interval.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID.

title: A failed sample keeps its own counter and is never a work retry
when: Makes two cleanup reads fail.
then: Expects the cleanup failure counter at 2 and the work retries counter unchanged.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryCleanup that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: An operation root keeps the supplied context's cancellation, deadline and ownership
when: Starts an operation root from a context with a deadline, a value and a parent span, then cancels the parent.
then: Expects the root context to keep the deadline and the value, to end when the parent is cancelled, and to have a new trace with no parent span.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetrySpans that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A database span is a child of the current operation
when: Runs a reconcile that calls the emitted store once.
then: Expects the database span's parent ID to equal the reconcile span's ID.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetrySpans that carries this ID. The store span starts from the provider of the operation span, as a generated store does. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: Sampling applies to each operation root
when: Runs one hundred reconciles at sampling ratio 0.5 with a deterministic ID source.
then: Expects each root sampled by its own trace ID, and the children of a root to share its decision.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetrySpans that carries this ID. The IDs come from a counter, under a sampled remote parent. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: A controller span or log carries no resource key, provider response, credential or private error text
when: Runs a reconcile on a key that holds a marker string and fails with an error whose text holds a second marker and a credential.
then: Expects no exported span attribute, event or log field that contains either marker or the credential.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetrySpans that carries this ID. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: Attribute and link counts per span stay within the default limits
when: Runs a reconcile that adds many attributes and links to its span.
then: Expects each exported span to hold at most the default limits of 128 attributes and 128 links.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetrySpans that carries this ID. The controller sets no span limit of its own, so the limits are the provider's; the test fails when the provider raises them. The spans are those of the real telemetry runtime, exported to the fake TLS gRPC trace collector on loopback; the meter and logger providers are the OpenTelemetry SDK with readers in memory, which the runtime would hand on unfiltered.

title: Without a collector, completion logs go to standard error
when: Runs one reconcile that succeeds and one that fails with no collector endpoint, capturing standard error.
then: Expects two JSON lines with the operation, the outcome and the retry flag, and no key or error text.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestTelemetryExport that carries this ID. The telemetry runtime is the real one with no collector endpoint; the test reads the standard error writer of the owner. Each line carries the trace and span IDs that the runtime gives with no collector, and the two reconciles have their own traces. A second subtest stalls standard error: the controller still finishes, the lines beyond the queue are dropped and counted, and the close ends within its limit.

title: The runtime starts no provider without a collector
when: Creates the runtime with no collector endpoint and wraps a handler.
then: Expects no tracer provider and the handler served directly, also after Close.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestWithoutCollector that carries this ID. It starts the runtime with no telemetry setting.

title: The runtime starts while the collector never answers
when: Creates the runtime against a collector that accepts the connection and never answers.
then: Expects creation to succeed before any export completes.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestExportConnection that carries this ID. It uses a loopback listener that accepts and never answers.

title: A disabled runtime returns the caller context unchanged
when: Starts an RPC trace on a closed runtime and on a runtime with no provider.
then: Expects the caller context returned unchanged.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestExportConnection that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: A full queue does not block the request
when: Serves three times the queue size of requests while the collector never answers.
then: Expects every request answered in under one second.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestQueuesDoNotBlock that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback, held.

title: The runtime counts export failures per signal
when: Records calls and flushes while the trace, metric and log collectors never answer.
then: Expects the metric and log failure counters to rise and a forced flush to report failure.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestExportFailures that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback, held.

title: The span carries the status the client received
when: Serves handlers that send informational, upgrade and final statuses in different orders through a real server.
then: Expects the span status field to equal the status on the wire for every order.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestHTTPSpan that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory recorders of the test harness and a real HTTP server, so the status is the one on the wire.

title: The span names the registered route and not the path
when: Serves a registered route whose handler writes and flushes twice.
then: Expects the span named by the method and the pattern with three attributes, and the private path absent from the export.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestHTTPSpan that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The RPC span lasts until the final status
when: Starts an RPC trace for each gRPC status code and finishes it with that status.
then: Expects a valid span context during the call, no span ended before finish, and one server span ended after it.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCSpan that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The RPC span carries three fields and a fixed failure class
when: Starts an RPC trace for each gRPC status code and finishes it with that status.
then: Expects exactly three attributes, a fourth error.type and an error status only for the six failure codes, and an empty status description.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCSpan that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The RPC span holds no private call data
when: Starts an RPC trace with private metadata, baggage, a trace state and a private status message.
then: Expects no attribute value, event, link or trace state that holds a private value.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCSpan that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: Code that holds the server span adds no event, attribute, status message, name or span
when: Serves an HTTP request and an RPC call whose handler calls RecordError, AddEvent, SetAttributes, SetStatus with a message and SetName on the server span, and starts a span of its own with the span's provider; then adds 67 probe events to one span through SpanEvent.
then: Expects only the HTTP and the RPC span exported, with none of the handler's data, no status message, no link and the probe event only; and 64 events kept and three reported dropped.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the two subtests of TestSpanOwnData that carry this ID. It uses the in-memory recorders of the test harness behind the runtime's own span processor.

title: The metrics count unsampled calls and link sampled ones
when: Serves one HTTP request and one RPC call with the sampling ratio 1, and again with the ratio 0.
then: Expects one count in each histogram in both runs, exemplars that carry the call's trace and span IDs at ratio 1, and no exported span at ratio 0.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestSignals that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The runtime logs one correlated completion per call
when: Serves one denied HTTP request and one denied RPC call.
then: Expects one log record per call with the fixed event name, WARN severity, four fields, both timestamps and the trace and span IDs of that call.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestSignals that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The metrics and logs hold no private data
when: Serves calls with a private path, query, token, baggage and error text.
then: Expects none of those values in the exported logs or metrics.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestSignals that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The server span starts before authentication and capacity admission
when: Serves one HTTP request and one RPC call that authentication refuses, and one that capacity admission refuses.
then: Expects a server span for each, with a start time before the refusal, and the final status 401 or 503 on it.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestServerSpanBounds that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The server span ends only after the final status is known
when: Serves an HTTP handler that writes the header and then streams the body, and an RPC call that ends with a status.
then: Expects each span to end after the last byte and to carry the final status.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestServerSpanBounds that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The span wrapper does not change the observed call
when: Serves the same requests with telemetry on and off, including a refused authentication, a capacity refusal, a stream that expires and a shutdown during a call.
then: Expects the same status, headers, body, deadlines and shutdown order in both runs.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestServerSpanBounds that carries this ID. It uses a real HTTP server, once with the fake TLS gRPC collector and once with no collector. The two runs are compared whole, so a changed deadline is caught.

title: Health and discovery routes stay outside the request wrappers
when: Sends requests to /livez, /readyz and the three public discovery routes: <base>/openapi, <base>/openapi.html and the metadata route at <base>.
then: Expects no span, no request metric sample and no completion log for any of the five requests.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestServerSpanBounds that carries this ID. It builds the assembler's shape: a top router holds the five public routes and mounts Handler on /. The base path is /v1, so a wrapper that exempts only the root paths is caught, and an encoded slash (/v1%2Fopenapi) must reach the wrapped application and be observed.

title: A single valid traceparent continues its trace and parent
when: Sends a request with one valid traceparent header.
then: Expects the server span to have the header's trace ID and the header's span ID as its parent.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestParentAndSampling that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The remote sampled flag does not change the local ratio decision
when: Sends requests with the sampled flag set and cleared at local ratios 0, 0.5 and 1, with fixed trace IDs.
then: Expects the sampling decision to equal the ratio decision for the trace ID in every case.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestParentAndSampling that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments. The test works out the ratio rule itself, not through the SDK sampler.

title: With a collector endpoint and no exporter setting all three signals are enabled
when: Builds the settings with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set and no exporter variable.
then: Expects traces, metrics and request logs enabled.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestSettings that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The settings defaults are ratio 0.1, a ten-second interval and the declared service name
when: Builds the settings with only the endpoint set.
then: Expects sampling ratio 0.1, metric export interval 10 s and the declared service name.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestSettings that carries this ID. It reads the settings from a fixed environment.

title: A protocol setting other than grpc is refused
when: Builds the settings with the protocol absent, grpc, http/protobuf and http/json.
then: Expects the first two accepted and the last two refused with an error that names the setting.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestSettings that carries this ID. It reads the settings from a fixed environment.

title: The certificate setting is read only as a bounded regular PEM file
when: Points the certificate setting at a valid PEM file, a directory, a symbolic link to a device, a file larger than the bound and a non-PEM file; then leaves it absent.
then: Expects the PEM file used, each other case refused, and the system roots used when the setting is absent.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestSettings that carries this ID. It reads the trust roots from files in a temporary folder and from the system.

title: The trace queue holds at most 256 spans in batches of at most 32
when: Blocks the fake collector and ends 300 spans, then releases the collector.
then: Expects every span either exported or counted as dropped (300 in total), at most 288 exported (the queue and one batch held by the blocked export), at least 12 dropped, and no batch larger than 32.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestExportLimits that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback, held and then released. The test does not assert an exact dropped count: the batch held by the blocked export call is outside the queue.

title: Each export ends within two seconds with a 64 KiB response limit
when: Makes the fake collector hold an export for five seconds, then answer with a 65 KiB response.
then: Expects the held export cancelled at two seconds and the large response refused.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtest of TestExportLimits that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback, held for five seconds, then padded responses of 64,512 and 66,560 bytes.

title: Shutdown gives the provider at most three seconds
when: Blocks the fake collector and calls shutdown.
then: Expects shutdown to return within three seconds and a short margin.
notes: Level: integration. Automated: the subtests of TestExportLimits that carry this ID. They use the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback, held. The first asserts that each span is exported or counted dropped; the second that Shutdown ends by the earlier of the caller's deadline and three seconds. TestSpanQueueShutdownRace (under ST-SUP-RP03-LC10-T01) proves that a span that ends during shutdown is queued or counted.

title: The request duration histograms have fixed names, unit, boundaries and temporality
when: Serves one HTTP request and one RPC call and collects the metrics.
then: Expects http.server.request.duration and rpc.server.call.duration as histograms with the unit s, the explicit boundaries 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60, 300 and 1800, and cumulative temporality.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestMetrics that carries this ID. It uses the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The duration labels are only method, route, status and error class
when: Serves requests to two routes with path values, one success and one failure.
then: Expects the attribute keys to equal the fixed set, the route to be the registered pattern, and the error class to be one of the fixed values.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestMetrics that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The active request counters carry no label
when: Holds one HTTP request and one RPC call open and collects the metrics.
then: Expects http.server.active_requests and rpc.server.active_requests as up-down counters at 1 with no attribute.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestMetrics that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: No metric label holds a trace or span ID
when: Serves a sampled request and collects the metrics.
then: Expects no attribute value equal to the request's trace ID or span ID.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRequestMetrics that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments. Exemplars are allowed; only labels are checked.

title: The completion log has the fixed name and the span's fields
when: Serves one HTTP request and one RPC call.
then: Expects one log named http.server.request.completed and one named rpc.server.call.completed, each with the span's fields, the duration and the trace and span IDs.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestCompletionLogs that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The request completion log severity follows the request outcome
when: Serves HTTP requests answered 200, 403, 400 and 500; then RPC calls that end with OK, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT and INTERNAL.
then: Expects INFO, WARN, WARN and ERROR in that order for the HTTP requests, and INFO, WARN, WARN and ERROR in that order for the RPC calls.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestCompletionLogs that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The completion log of a failed call holds its fixed error code and no error text
when: Serves one HTTP request and one RPC call that the handler fails with the fixed code internal and an error whose text holds an email, one denied with the code denied, and one that passes.
then: Expects the completion log of each failed or denied call to hold its fixed error code and not the email or other error text, and the log of the passing call to hold no error code.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestCompletionLogs that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments. Each handler gives a code that holds the error text first, which SetErrorCode ignores, and then its fixed code; the passing calls give a code too, which their logs do not hold. The code is the log attribute error.code. Mutations caught: no code in the log, a code of any form taken, a code on a passing call, no code place on an RPC call.

title: The RPC span records exactly the three fixed attributes
when: Serves one RPC call for each of the seventeen gRPC status codes.
then: Expects each span to carry exactly rpc.system.name, rpc.method and rpc.response.status_code, the last equal to the status name.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCAttributes that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: Only the six server statuses mark the RPC span failed
when: Serves one RPC call for each of the seventeen gRPC status codes.
then: Expects the span status error with error.type equal to the status name for UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE and DATA_LOSS, and not error for the other eleven.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCAttributes that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: No server span carries a resource ID, a user identity, a peer address or error text
when: Serves HTTP and RPC calls with a marker in the path, in the identity, in the peer address and in the error text.
then: Expects no exported span attribute or event that contains any marker.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRPCAttributes that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The route pattern survives a copied request
when: Serves a request whose authentication middleware replaces the request with a copy.
then: Expects the span, the metric and the log to carry the registered pattern.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRoutePattern that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: The route pattern is kept at sampling ratio zero
when: Serves a request at sampling ratio 0.
then: Expects the metric and the log to carry the registered pattern.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRoutePattern that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: Metrics and logs do not take their fields from recorded span attributes
when: Serves a request whose handler sets a span attribute with the key of a metric label to a marker value.
then: Expects no metric label and no log field equal to the marker.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestRoutePattern that carries this ID. It uses the in-memory span, metric and log recorders of the test harness, with the runtime's own sampler, limits and instruments.

title: An operation span of a registered name is exported with its own record
when: Registers the names reconcile and scan, starts a root reconcile span and a child scan span, adds a fill attribute and an error message through the SDK span, and finishes both with outcome failure.
then: Expects both spans exported, the child under the root, only the fixed attributes, an error status with an empty description, and no fill attribute.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestOperationSpan that carries this ID. It runs on the test harness of the runtime with an SDK span recorder behind the runtime's own span processor; it also checks that SpanEvent accepts the child span. Further subtests that carry this ID: a span that the caller ends early keeps its outcome, status and end time; SpanEvent refuses a zero key and free-text names and keys; spans that never end are bounded at SpanRecordLimit and counted; without a provider an operation still gets IDs, and Registered follows New.

title: An unregistered span name is refused
when: Starts an operation span with a name not registered at start.
then: Expects an error and no span exported.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestOperationSpan that carries this ID. It also refuses a span with no parent choice and an invalid name at New.

title: The probe runtime starts a child span per call
when: Starts the telemetry runtime with the probe's span names, binds two calls to a sampled server span, emits an event in each, commits one and rolls back the other.
then: Expects each call bound to its own child span of the server span, the event on that child span and not on the server span, and the outcomes committed and rolled_back on the two child spans.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeCallSpan that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. The rolled-back call span is not marked as an error. A second subtest starts the probe on a runtime without the call span name: Start fails with an error that names it.

title: A Tenant is built only through the one constructor from its three sources
when: Reads the exported API of the package with go/types, then calls the constructor with a verified identity that holds a tenant claim and one that holds none.
then: Expects one exported constructor that takes a source, sources only from an Identity, the row reader and a Decision, no exported field or conversion that builds a Tenant from a string, a Tenant for the first call and an error for the second.
notes: Level: unit. The test type-checks the package source with go/types: Source has only unexported methods, Claim and Requested are the only functions that give a Source, Identity and Decision are interfaces of github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/internal/seal with an unexported method, ScanRows (the row reader) reads a *sql.Rows, and no exported type is a Source. Re-review of PR #144: a tenant ID with NUL, DEL, U+0085, U+202E, U+200B, U+2028, U+2029 or U+FEFF is refused through Claim and through Requested.

title: Every function that takes a Tenant refuses the zero value before any statement
when: Calls each exported function of the package that takes a Tenant with the zero value, against a database fake that records statements.
then: Expects an error from each function and no recorded statement.
notes: Level: unit. The test finds the functions that take a Tenant with go/types over the package API, so a new function without the check is caught, and calls each against a database/sql fake that records statements.

title: A client-supplied header or body field is not accepted as a tenant source
when: Sends a request with X-Tenant-ID and a body field tenant_id set to tenant B, under a verified identity of tenant A.
then: Expects the tenant in the context to be A.
notes: Level: service. The request goes through the library's Middleware; the verifier that the service passes it is a local stand-in for the generated authentication component, and the generated component's own proof is ST-SUP-RC20-OC35.

title: A worker gets its tenant only from the tenant list or the outbox row
when: Builds a Tenant from an entry of the tenant list through the iterator, from a claimed outbox row of tenant t2, and from a message payload whose member tenant is t9.
then: Expects the first two to give t1 and t2 through the one constructor, and the payload to be refused as a source with no Tenant built.
notes: Level: integration. A table outbox_stand_in stands in for the outbox runtime's queue table, which is not built yet. The payload is refused at type-checking: New takes only a Source, and a call with the decoded payload or its member tenant does not type-check. Runs against the local PostgreSQL 17.7 server (image postgres:17.7, digest sha256:2006493727bd5277eece187319af1ef82b4cf82cf4fc1ed00da0775b646ac2a4) of pgtest (ST-SUP-TOOL14): the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, a superuser URL, else a container without privilege that the test binary starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL-R04); the test makes its own database, owner role and runtime role with the table items under row-level security and the tenant list of Migration, and drops them at the end. The runtime CI job runs it against the container. Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error. Decision of 2026-11-07 on the review of PR 125, under the Product owner's delegation.

title: Identity and Decision are sealed to the runtime module
when: Builds a test module outside the runtime module that declares its own types with the exported methods of Identity and of Decision and passes each to the constructor.
then: Expects the build to fail for each of the two types, with an error for the missing unexported method.
notes: Level: unit. The test type-checks, with go/types, a package outside the runtime module that declares the two types and passes each to the constructor; go/types reports the missing unexported method as the build does.

title: A tenant column becomes a Tenant only through the row reader
when: Reads the tenant column of one row of stego_tenants and of one outbox row through the row reader, then tries every other exported function of the package with the same text.
then: Expects a Tenant from each row read, and no other exported function that gives a Tenant from the text.
notes: Level: integration. A table outbox_stand_in stands in for the outbox runtime's queue table. The test finds the other exported functions with go/types and expects none that gives a Tenant from text. Runs against the local PostgreSQL 17.7 server (image postgres:17.7, digest sha256:2006493727bd5277eece187319af1ef82b4cf82cf4fc1ed00da0775b646ac2a4) of pgtest (ST-SUP-TOOL14): the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, a superuser URL, else a container without privilege that the test binary starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL-R04); the test makes its own database, owner role and runtime role and drops them at the end. The runtime CI job runs it against the container. Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error.

title: An outer type cannot change the tenant of a genuine Identity or Decision
when: Outside the runtime module, declares a type that embeds a genuine authn.Identity of tenant t1 and declares TenantClaim() to give t2; a type that embeds a nil tenant.Identity interface; a type that embeds a genuine Decision for t1 and declares Allowed() to give true for t2; and the zero values of Identity, Decision and the two marks; and passes each to tenant.Claim or tenant.Requested.
then: Expects the first to give t1 only, the Decision case to give t1 only and refuse t2, and every nil or zero value to give no tenant, with no panic.
notes: Level: unit. A genuine authn.Identity of t1 comes from authn.Verify of a token minted by authn/authntest; the genuine Decision for t1 is the test's stand-in of the authorization runtime, made with seal.NewDecisionMark (the authorization runtime is not built yet). Go gives an outer type the same method set in any package, so the forged types run in the test package; ST-SUP-RP13-LC01-T03 type-checks the forged Identity outside the runtime module. A nil embedded pointer of authn.Identity and the nil values give no tenant too. Each case fails on the code of PR #144 before the review: it read TenantClaim and Allowed. Mutation check: the test fails when the check it proves is removed or weakened (mutate.py in the builder's notes, 84 mutations, all killed). Security review of PR #144 (authentication runtime).

title: A Decision serves only the action and the tenant it was decided for
when: Gets a Decision from the authorization runtime for provision of tenant ta, then passes it to Requested for provision of ta, for retire of ta and for provision of tb; and gets one for retire of ta and passes it to Requested for provision of ta.
then: Expects a Tenant only for provision of ta from the first Decision, and only for retire of ta from the second, with no tenant for every other pair.
notes: Level: unit. Not automated yet: the code change of the review of PR #146 is not written yet. Planned file registry/runtime/tenant/tenant_test.go. Review of PR #146 (authorization runtime).

title: The context returns the tenant the authentication component set
when: Sets tenant A through the authentication path and reads the tenant from the context.
then: Expects tenant A and no error.
notes: Level: unit.

title: A context with no tenant returns an error and never a zero tenant
when: Reads the tenant from context.Background().
then: Expects an error and a zero Tenant that every Tenant-taking function refuses.
notes: Level: unit.

title: The first statement of every transaction sets the tenant transaction-locally
when: Opens two transactions through the helper with tenants A and B and runs one SELECT in each, with statement logging on.
then: Expects SELECT set_config('app.tenant', $1, true) as the first statement of each transaction with the matching tenant, before the caller's SELECT.
notes: Level: integration. The statement log is the client side log of pgx's query tracer, which records each statement that the connection sends, with begin and commit. The runtime CI job runs it against the container. Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error.

title: The helper runs no session-scoped tenant setting
when: Opens a transaction through the helper, commits, then reads current_setting('app.tenant', true) on the same connection.
then: Expects an empty value after the commit, and no SET or set_config with false in the statement log.
notes: Level: integration. The test also scans the string literals of the package source for a session-scoped SET and for set_config with is_local false. Runs against the local PostgreSQL 17.7 server (image postgres:17.7, digest sha256:2006493727bd5277eece187319af1ef82b4cf82cf4fc1ed00da0775b646ac2a4) of pgtest (ST-SUP-TOOL14): the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, a superuser URL, else a container without privilege that the test binary starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL-R04); the test makes its own database, owner role and runtime role with the table items under row-level security and the tenant list of Migration, and drops them at the end. The runtime CI job runs it against the container. Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error.

title: A transaction whose tenant setting changed does not commit
when: Opens a transaction for tenant A through the helper, runs set_config('app.tenant', 'B', true) as the caller's statement, writes one row and commits.
then: Expects the commit refused with an error that names no tenant value, the transaction rolled back, and no row.

title: A transfer and its entries are inserted in one statement
when: Posts a balanced transfer of two entries while a statement recorder reads every statement.
then: Expects the transfer row and both entry rows written by one statement.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestPost; its subtest carries this ID. It runs against the local PostgreSQL server of pgtest (ST-SUP-TOOL14): the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, else a container of postgres:17.7, pinned by digest, without privilege, that the test binary starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL-R04). Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error. The runtime CI job runs it against the container. The test makes a database of its own, owned by the owner role, applies the DDL text, the CHECK constraint of the declared transfer codes (as the generated migration does) and the lease runtime's leases table as the owner, opens each transaction with tenant.Begin and commits it with tenant.Commit. The statement recorder is pgx's query tracer on the client: it sees one call of ledger_post and no INSERT. then: Expects the checkpoint written with the holder's fencing token while the lease row still names the holder, and the lease row released after that write; expects no checkpoint write after the release.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestModeShutdown; its subtest carries this ID. It runs against the local PostgreSQL server of pgtest (ST-SUP-TOOL14): the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names, else a container of postgres:17.7, pinned by digest, without privilege, that the test binary starts and removes (ST-STD-LOCAL-R04). Without podman or docker the test fails; it skips only when STEGO_TEST_NO_CONTAINERS=1, and then says so on standard error. Use a real PostgreSQL with the leases table and a fake clock where the test needs time to pass. Decision on ST-SUP-Q37, reading A: every write under the lease carries the fencing token (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03), so the flush comes first. A sequencer that releases first writes the checkpoint with no valid token and fails the test. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

title: A periodic job runs at its interval only while the lease is held
when: Registers a job with a 1 s interval on a fake clock in controller mode, holds the lease, advances the clock three intervals, then loses the lease and advances again.

notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestPeriodic; its subtest carries this ID. The component runs in the controller mode of a modes.Registry. The lease is a real lease row of pgtest; it is lost when another holder takes the row and the renew fails. The fake clock moves only when the test advances it; 999 ms after a run no new run starts. The second run fails: it is counted and reported by Health, and the third runs. With the lease lost, and with no lease, a due run is skipped and counted. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest, which the suite starts and removes (pgtest). Review of PR #178: each run takes 300 ms of the process clock and the next starts 1 s after the last start; each run's deadline is the lease's expiry; after a skip the job tries again at the retry period, and runs at the first retry after the lease is acquired again.

title: The query handle gives the fill its bound probe, which goes quiet once the fill returns
when: Binds a handle for open-reservations with a probe on a recorder, tenant t1 and principal user:u-7; the fill emits reservation_lookup_empty through Probe, starts a goroutine that keeps the probe, and returns; the goroutine emits again before Run ends the transaction.
then: Expects one recorded emission with tenant t1, principal user:u-7 and operation open-reservations, and the emission from the goroutine dropped and counted.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestProbe; its subtest carries this ID. The transaction is a test double of a database/sql driver, because the probe does not touch storage, and the probe runtime's Recorder takes the emissions. A test hook makes the goroutine emit after the fill returned and before Run ends the transaction. A second subtest checks that Run refuses a probe call bound to another tenant, principal or query. Owner decision of 2026-11-06: a declared domain probe is the only sanctioned path for a fill to emit logs or domain signals.

title: The query handle offers no writer, logger or other probe
when: Lists the exported methods of query.Handle and of each value it returns by go/types.

The test also gives Evaluate and Send a value that new makes and a copy of a loaded value; each is refused with errForeignValue before the decision port, and the loaded value itself is sent. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. The test uses the real tenant, authz, outbox and audit runtimes: the pools come from tenant.Open, and the database holds the outbox queue, the authz tables, the audit tables and three tenant-owned entity tables with row-level security, read as a runtime role that is not a superuser. title: A change to a loaded value's copy does not reach a send
when: Reads a row with a slice field, changes an element of the slice that Value returned, and sends the loaded value.
then: Expects the stored element sent, not the changed one.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestLoaded; its subtest carries this ID. The slice field is a bytea column of the row. The fill changes the first byte of the note that Value returned, then sends the loaded value through Send of a stream query. A recording fake decision port stands behind the real authorization runtime. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names.
