The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: A streamed query sends allowed values only, each decided when it is sent
when: Binds a stream query handle for user:u-7, where the fake decision port allows view on o-1 and o-3 and denies it on o-2; the fill sends o-1, o-2 and o-3; then the decision port revokes view on o-3 with a newer token before the third send; then the fill sends after the stream ends.
then: Expects o-1 sent, o-2 dropped and counted, and in the second run o-3 dropped because the decision at the floor saw the revocation, and the send after the end to return an error and send nothing.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestStream; its subtest carries this ID. The fill lists the Orders on the query's list permission, which the fake port allows, and sends each; Send decides view. In the second run the test raises the floor in authz_floor to f9 before the third send, and the fake port denies o-3 only at least as fresh as f9, so a send that decided at the row token would send it. A send after RunStream returns, and a send after the stream's context ended, send nothing. A recording fake decision port stands behind the real authorization runtime. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. The test uses the real tenant, authz, outbox and audit runtimes: the pools come from tenant.Open, and the database holds the outbox queue, the authz tables, the audit tables and three tenant-owned entity tables with row-level security, read as a runtime role that is not a superuser. Decision on N3 of the re-check of PR 125 (2026-11-07, under the Product owner's delegation): gRPC server streams stay, each backed by a query fill with the read-only query handle and a decision on each message at the floor; client and bidirectional streams are out of scope for now and are refused.

title: The query runtime commits only through tenant.Commit
when: Scans the package's non-test files with go/types for calls of Commit on a *sql.Tx or on a type that wraps one, and calls the runtime's constructor with a *sql.DB from sql.Open.
then: Expects no such call outside tenant.Commit, and the pool refused with an error.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestRun; its subtest carries this ID. go/types type-checks the package source and lists each call of Commit on a *sql.Tx or on a type that holds one. New refuses a store pool and an audit pool of sql.Open and takes the pools of tenant.Open, through tenant.Opened (ST-SUP-RP04-LC08). PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names.

title: A changed or moved cursor is refused
when: Lists one page, then sends its cursor unchanged, with one byte changed, for another query, and for another tenant.
then: Expects the next page for the unchanged cursor, and a refusal with no rows read for each other case.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestCursor; its subtest carries this ID. The list query is served through Serve with httptest, two rows a page. The changed cursor has one byte of its position changed (a key that sorts later, so a cursor without the MAC would skip rows), or one byte of its MAC; the moved cursor goes to another list query, another tenant and another principal. Each refusal is 400 with no fill call and no decision, so no row is read. A search cursor keeps its page token and first consistency. A recording fake decision port stands behind the real authorization runtime. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest, which the suite starts and removes (pgtest). The test uses the real tenant, authz, outbox and audit runtimes: the pools come from tenant.Open, and the database holds the outbox queue, the authz tables, the audit tables and tenant-owned entity tables with row-level security, read as a runtime role that is not a superuser. Review of PR #178: the cursor is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key from HKDF-SHA256; the test decodes the text and checks that it shows no key, query, principal, provider name, provider cursor or token, and that another service with the same key opens no cursor. Re-review of PR #178: a cursor key with no service name is refused.

title: A failed read is audited with its code
when: Runs a pii read that succeeds and one whose decision fails, and reads the audit rows.
then: Expects no error_code on the first row and the fixed code on the second, with no error text.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestReadAuditCode; its subtest carries this ID. The fake decision port is down for the second read. The test reads the read rows of audit_event: the first has outcome ok and no error code, the second outcome failed, the code undecided and no state, and no row holds the provider's error text or a field of the row. RecordRead refuses an error text as a code. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest, which the suite starts and removes (pgtest). The test uses the real tenant, authz, outbox and audit runtimes: the pools come from tenant.Open, and the database holds the outbox queue, the authz tables, the audit tables and tenant-owned entity tables with row-level security, read as a runtime role that is not a superuser.

title: One helper serves get and list
when: Serves a get and a list query through the helper with httptest, including a denied row and a bad cursor.
then: Expects 200 with the rows, 404 for the denied row, and 400 for the bad cursor, each as a problem response with no row data.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestServe; its subtest carries this ID. The get and list queries are served with httptest; the fake decision port denies order o2. A problem response holds only type, title and status, with no row data. The test also checks 400 for a request that does not decode, 401 for a failed bind, 405 for a POST, and that a list helper needs the cursor key. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at a pinned image digest, which the suite starts and removes (pgtest). The test uses the real tenant, authz, outbox and audit runtimes: the pools come from tenant.Open, and the database holds the outbox queue, the authz tables, the audit tables and tenant-owned entity tables with row-level security, read as a runtime role that is not a superuser. Review of PR #178: also a list whose provider fails is 503, a body above MaxRequestBody is 400 with no more read, and every response has Cache-Control: no-store. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q84, ST-SUP-Q81): TestServeHelpers in registry/runtime/query/helpers_test.go, whose subtest carries this ID too, proves the helpers that moved into the runtime (the refusal lookup is proved under ST-SUP-RP11-LC17-T02): BindHTTP binds a token that the verifier passed to the tenant of its claim, the user subject, the query's probe call and a request ID that the server makes, not the X-Request-Id header of the request (ST-SUP-Q105 option a, the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation, 2026-11-11), and a request with no verified identity is 401; Limit and EncodePage read the limit parameter and write the page body with no total; and Row.Int32, Row.Float, Row.Bytes and Row.JSON read their column kinds. Mutations caught: an unbounded limit, an unbounded Int32 (the refusal mutations are under ST-SUP-RP11-LC17-T02). A bind with no tenant check is not caught: the verifier refuses a token with no tenant claim first. The checks of the generated query service (internal/generator/query/testdata/query_test.go) also send get-order on an order whose fill returns the declared refusal order_unknown, which the generated lookup queries.Declared answers with 404 and the code order.unknown; mutation caught: no refusal lookup in the generated handler.

title: Serve answers a refusal that the lookup knows with its status and code, and another error with 500 internal
when: Serves a get query through query.HTTP with a refusal lookup that knows order_unknown as 404 order.unknown, with a fill that returns order_unknown, then one that returns another error whose text holds an email, then with no lookup.
then: Expects 404 with the code order.unknown in the problem response and in the completion log; 500 with the code internal and no email for the other error; and 500 internal for the refusal when no lookup is set.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by the subtest of this ID in TestServeHelpers. The completion log's code is read through otel.WithErrorCode and otel.ErrorCode, as the telemetry runtime's Handler gives the place of it. The test also checks that a refusal of another query and one that a fill made itself are 500 internal. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names (ST-STD-LOCAL). The orchestrator decided under the owner's delegation (2026-11-11, ST-SUP-Q95, option a) that the code goes to the problem response and the completion log only, not to the read audit row, which is written when the fill reads the row (ST-SUP-RP11-LC08). Mutations caught: the lookup ignored, no code to the completion log.

title: A list in a field order with equal values gives every row once over its pages
when: Lists 250 rows of one tenant, many with equal values of the order field, by that field descending with a page limit of 7, follows each cursor to the end, and lists by a field that the entity does not declare.
then: Expects every row once in the order of the field and then the key, no total in a page, and the undeclared field refused with no rows read.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestListOrder; its subtest carries this ID. 250 orders of t1 hold nine values of total; the fake decision port denies each order whose key ends in 3, so the list keeps only allowed rows. Each page goes through CursorText and ParseCursor, so the sealed cursor carries the position of total and of the key. The test also lists by two fields in two directions, the first one with NULL values, which come last; checks that a page holds only Items, Next and More; that an undeclared field, a text that is not a column and a field given twice are refused with no statement run; and that a cursor of one order is refused for another order. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest: the local container of its pinned image, which the test binary starts and removes, or the server that STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names (ST-STD-LOCAL). Mutations caught: no key tie-breaker, the direction ignored, NULLs first, the rows after a NULL position dropped, an undeclared field taken, the cursor's order not checked, the cursor without its position values, a cursor of the key order taken in an ordered list.

title: One helper serves a get, a list and a stream over gRPC as Serve does over HTTP
when: Serves a get query over ServeRPC with a fill that reads an order and a charge with personal data, and calls it on an allowed order, a denied order, a missing order, with an empty ID, with no identity, with a declared refusal and with a fill that fails; serves a list query one row a page and pages it with the cursor of each response, then with a bad cursor and with a provider that is down; serves a stream query over ServeStream and opens it, then with a bad request, with no identity, with a fill that fails and with a send that the transport refuses.
then: Expects the allowed get answered with the JSON body of the HTTP handler read into the response message and one read audit row of the charge; the denied and missing orders NotFound with no data of the row; the empty ID InvalidArgument and the call with no identity Unauthenticated, neither reaching the fill; the refusal NotFound with its code; the failed fill Internal with the code internal and no error text; the pages to hold the allowed rows only, the bad cursor InvalidArgument before the fill, and the provider that is down Unavailable; the stream to send the allowed values only, the refused streams to send nothing with InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and Internal, and the refused send to end the stream with the transport's status.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestServeRPC; its subtest carries this ID. The messages are the well-known types google.protobuf.StringValue and google.protobuf.Struct, so the test needs no generated code; a recording fake decision port stands behind the real authorization runtime, which allows every order but o2. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 through pgtest, without privilege. Mutations caught: a deny answered PermissionDenied, the list cursor of the request not read, the error text in the status, a stream that ignores a bad request, a declared refusal not looked up, a failed send not given to the client.

title: The request ID of a query call is made on the server, never taken from the client
when: Binds a query twice through BindHTTP with a verified token and the header X-Request-Id client-chosen-id, twice through BindRPC with the metadata x-request-id client-chosen-id, and once through BindContext with no request ID.
then: Expects each bound call to carry a new UUID as its request ID, never client-chosen-id, and no two the same.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestRequestID; its subtest carries this ID. The token is verified by the runtime verifier with a local key (authntest). Run uses the request ID of the bound call for each read audit row, and makes a new one when the bound call has none. ST-SUP-Q105 option a, decided by the orchestrator under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11). Mutations caught: BindHTTP takes the X-Request-Id header, BindContext keeps an empty request ID (mut/round2.json of b-rt-harden).

title: The emit function has no message or free attribute parameter
when: Lists the exported functions and methods of the package by go/types.
then: Expects the emit function to take a descriptor and typed values only, and no string message, format string, error, map or attribute parameter.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSurface that carries this ID. It reads the package with go/types from the export data of go list.

title: An emission with a value of the wrong kind or count, or a measure out of range, is dropped
when: Emits reservation_refused, whose fields are sku (read from a loaded Reservation), reason (enum) and qty (measure 1..1000), with one value; then with qty 0; then with qty 1001; then with every value right, to a recorder.
then: Expects one recorded emission only, and the drop count to rise by three.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBinding that carries this ID. It also emits a value of the wrong kind, an enum value outside its set and an emission from another emitter, each dropped and counted.

title: A probe reports the call it was bound to and offers no way to change it
when: Binds a probe to a span context, tenant t1, principal user:u-7 and the command reserve-and-charge, and lists the exported methods of the probe by reflection.
then: Expects the bound values back, and no setter, no exported field and no method that takes a span context, a tenant, a principal or an operation name.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBinding that carries this ID. It lists the methods with go/types, not reflection, as the other surface tests do.

title: A probe goes quiet once the fill returns
when: Binds a probe to a recorder, lets a fill start a goroutine that keeps the probe, returns from the fill as the generated code sees it, and emits reservation_refused from the goroutine before and after the end of the transaction.
then: Expects no recorded emission from the goroutine and each attempt counted.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBinding that carries this ID. It also checks the muted probe of another emitter.

title: A log record carries the opaque tenant and principal, and the span event and the metric carry neither
when: Binds a probe to a recording span of a test tracer, tenant t1, principal user:u-7 with the claims name and email, and reserve-and-charge, and emits the event reservation_refused and the counter reservations_refused to an in-memory log, span and metric exporter.
then: Expects the log record to carry domain.reservation_refused, the span's trace ID and span ID, t1, user:u-7 and reserve-and-charge, and no name, email or other claim; the span event to carry only the attributes sku and reason; and the metric to carry only reason and the operation.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBinding that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback; the recording span is the server span of a request that the telemetry runtime's Handler serves. Both observations count committed work, so the span event and the metric carry no stego.outcome; ST-SUP-RP12-LC13-T01 proves the sets of an observation that counts each attempt. The claims are in the context, where the probe does not read them. The bound span is the call's own child span of the server span (ST-SUP-RP03-LC15).

title: An event becomes one log record and one event on the recording span
when: With an in-memory log exporter on the telemetry runtime, emits reservation_refused(sku=A-1, reason=short) on a recording span; then on a span that is not sampled.
then: Expects one log record named domain.reservation_refused with severity WARN, the attributes sku=A-1 and reason=short and no body for each emission, and one span event of the same name and attributes on the recording span only.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeOTLP that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback; the recording span is the server span of a request that the telemetry runtime's Handler serves. The span that is not sampled is a valid remote span context with no sampled flag.

title: A counter adds one and a histogram records its value in its unit
when: With an in-memory metric reader on the telemetry runtime, emits the counter reservations_refused(reason=short) three times and the histogram reservation_wait(wait=12.5) once.
then: Expects domain.reservations_refused to be 3 with the attributes reason=short and operation=reserve-and-charge, and domain.reservation_wait to hold one value 12.5 in ms.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeOTLP that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. It reads the last cumulative export after Close.

title: OTLP is on only with a collector endpoint
when: Starts the runtime with no collector endpoint, then with one, and emits one event each time to an in-memory receiver on that endpoint.
then: Expects no OTLP record in the first case and one in the second.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSinks that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback.

title: The console sink writes one JSON or logfmt line per emission to standard output
when: Runs the test binary again as a child process with STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=json, then logfmt, emits one event, one counter and one histogram, and reads the child's standard output and standard error.
then: Expects three lines on standard output, each with timestamp, severity, service.name, service.instance.id, event.name, the fields, the value for the histogram, trace_id, span_id, tenant, principal and operation, and nothing on standard error.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeConsole that carries this ID. The child process runs the same subtest with Start, which reads the real environment and standard output.

title: A blocked sink does not block or fail the emission
when: Holds the console writer inside one write and emits three times the queue size of events from a fill, which then returns.
then: Expects every emission and the fill to return while the writer is still held, with no result and no panic, and the response of the call to be the same as with the console sink off.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSinks that carries this ID. One call holds at most 64 emissions (ST-SUP-RP12-LC20), so the three times the queue size come from 48 fills of 64 emissions.

title: A probe sends no private value and cuts long text
when: Emits reservation_refused with a sku of 1,000 bytes, from a context that holds a request path, an Authorization header and baggage, to a recorder and the console sink.
then: Expects the sku cut to 256 bytes of valid UTF-8, and no path, header, baggage, error text or stack in any record.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeValues that carries this ID. The sku is 334 euro signs, so the cut falls inside a rune; a second value holds an invalid byte and a NUL.

title: The recorder keeps every emission in order from concurrent callers
when: Emits 10,000 observations from 16 goroutines to one recorder, then reads the recorder.
then: Expects 10,000 emissions, each goroutine's in its call order, no drop, no race under the race detector, and no record in any other sink.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeRecorder that carries this ID. A runtime with a console writer is open beside the recorder and gets its own one emission and none of the recorder's. CI runs it under the race detector.

title: A fill test ends the call with a rollback and sees the rolled_back attempt
when: Binds a probe with the generated test constructor to a recorder, emits reservation_refused (attempt) and reservations_made (committed), and ends the call with a rollback; then does the same and ends it with a commit.
then: Expects, after the rollback, reservation_refused with stego.outcome=rolled_back and no reservations_made; after the commit, both, reservation_refused with stego.outcome=committed.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeRecorder that carries this ID. The test binds the recorder as the generated test constructor does, with a fixed tenant, principal and emitter name.

title: A fill test passes or fails on the recorded emission
when: With a recorder that holds reservation_refused(sku=A-1, reason=short): checks for reservation_refused with reason=short; then with reason=expired; then checks that reservation_refused was not emitted, each with a test double for testing.T.
then: Expects the first check to pass, and the second and the third to fail the test double with a message that names reservation_refused and lists the recorded emission.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeRecorder that carries this ID.

title: Close drains the console queue inside the shared shutdown budget
when: Queues 500 events for the console sink, then calls Close; then holds standard output in one write while a collector does not answer, and calls Close on a new runtime; then emits after Close.
then: Expects all 500 lines written before Close returns, the second Close to return inside the one shared shutdown limit of ST-SUP-RC17-OC29 and not after a second budget, and the emission after Close dropped and counted.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSinks that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. The second Close must return inside the shared limit of three seconds plus one second.

title: A span event and a metric hold no tenant, principal, trace ID or span ID
when: Emits reservation_refused and reservations_refused on a recording span for tenant t1 and principal user:u-7, with in-memory span and metric exporters.
then: Expects the span event's attributes to be exactly sku, reason and stego.outcome, and the metric's to be exactly reason, stego.outcome and operation.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeOTLP that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback; the recording span is the server span of a request that the telemetry runtime's Handler serves. The metric must have one data point.

title: The probe opens no provider or connection of its own
when: Starts the probe runtime with a telemetry runtime and records the providers and the connections the process opens.
then: Expects the probe to use the telemetry runtime's providers only, and no new provider, exporter or connection.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeOTLP that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. It counts the connections that the collector accepts, and reads the imports of the package source for an SDK, exporter or network package.

title: A domain histogram uses the fixed boundaries of its unit and cumulative temporality
when: Emits one histogram in each of the units s, ms, By and 1 to an in-memory metric reader, and reads the instruments.
then: Expects each instrument to hold the fixed boundaries of its unit and cumulative temporality.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeOTLP that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. The boundaries of s are compared with the exported http.server.request.duration of the telemetry runtime.

title: Domain observations reach the console only when the environment turns it on
when: Starts the runtime with no settings; with STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=json; with logfmt; with off; with a collector endpoint and no console setting; and with STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=yaml; and emits one declared event each time.
then: Expects no console line for the event, then a json line, then a logfmt line, then none, then none, and a start that fails with fixed error text that does not hold yaml.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSinks that carries this ID. It reads the setting from the process environment and gives the start a writer in memory.

title: No probe, fill or declaration input chooses a sink
when: Lists the exported API of the package and of a generated probe by go/types.
then: Expects no function, method or field that takes a sink, a writer or a format, other than the start of the runtime and Recorder.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSurface that carries this ID. The generated probe is a fixture in the test in the shape of ST-SUP-RC34-OC01 to ST-SUP-RC34-OC06, compiled against the package; ST-SUP-RC34-OC05-T01 proves the probe that the generator emits.

title: The console sink starts no provider and opens no connection
when: Starts the runtime with no collector endpoint and STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=json, and emits ten events.
then: Expects no OpenTelemetry provider and no connection opened, as ST-SUP-RP03-LC01 states.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeConsole that carries this ID. It counts the sockets of the process in /proc/self/fd before and after.

title: Drops and write failures are counted by sink
when: Holds the console writer, emits three times the queue size of events, then makes the writer fail once, with an in-memory metric reader.
then: Expects domain.probe.dropped with sink=console to equal the records beyond the bound, domain.probe.failed with sink=console to be 1, and no other label.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the two subtests of TestProbeSinks that carry this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback; the recording span is the server span of a request that the telemetry runtime's Handler serves. In the first, the first record is held inside the write before the burst, so the drops are exactly 2,048. In the second, two calls of 64 events on one server span each keep their events on their own call span (ST-SUP-RP03-LC15), and the otlp drop count stays 0.

title: A refusal that rolls back is sent, and committed work only after a commit
when: Binds a probe for reserve-and-charge to a recorder through the sinks, emits the event reservation_refused and the counter reservations_refused, which count each attempt, and the counter reservations_made, which counts committed work, then rolls back; then does the same and commits; then emits 65 events in one call.
then: Expects, after the rollback, reservation_refused and reservations_refused with stego.outcome=rolled_back and no reservations_made; after the commit, all three, the first two with stego.outcome=committed; and 64 records and one counted drop for the last call.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeSinks that carries this ID.

title: The service events are built-in observations on the probe's sinks
when: Starts the runtime with an in-memory log exporter and no console setting, sends service.ready and service.failed, and declares an observation named service.ready.
then: Expects one console line and one log record for each event with its fixed name and severity and no fields, and the declaration refused by name.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBuiltins that carries this ID. It uses the real telemetry runtime with the fake TLS gRPC collector on loopback. It also records the worker observations and drops an undeclared worker.

title: Built-in service events are on the console in every setting
when: Runs the test binary again as a child process with no settings; with STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=off; with a collector endpoint; and with STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE=logfmt; and sends service.ready each time.
then: Expects one JSON line for service.ready on standard output in each case, in the same fixed form, with no tenant, principal or entity value, and a log record at the collector in the third case.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the two subtests of TestProbeBuiltins that carry this ID. The child process runs the same subtest with Start; in the collector case it starts the fake collector itself and writes the count of log records to a file; each child also writes the line of telemetry.runtime.stopped that Close sends. The second subtest fills the queue of declared observations and expects service.ready on the console all the same.

title: The schema backfill observations are built in and their names are reserved
when: Emits each schema backfill observation with the open change user-email-rename to a recorder, reads the enum of the field change for a declaration with one open and one finished change, and declares an observation named schema.backfill.rows.
then: Expects each emission with its fixed name, kind, severity and the field change only, the enum to hold the open change alone, and the declaration refused by name.
notes: Level: unit. Automated: the subtest of TestProbeBuiltins that carries this ID. It emits through the lease runtime's Observer interface, and a finished change is dropped and counted.

title: Only Verify makes an Identity, and the Identity is sealed
when: Lists the exported functions, methods and types of the package by go/types, and type-checks a package outside the runtime module that declares a type with Identity's exported methods and passes it to tenant.Claim.
then: Expects Verify to be the only function that makes an Identity (FromContext gives back only the Identity that Middleware put in the context after Verify), Identity to have no setter, and the outside package to fail to type-check for the missing seal method.
notes: Level: unit. The test type-checks the package source with go/types: the exported functions and methods that give an Identity are Verify and FromContext, which makes none and gives back only the Identity that Middleware or Authenticate put in the context after Verify (ST-SUP-RP13-LC14-T01, LC20-T01). Identity has no exported field and no method with a parameter or a pointer receiver. A package outside the runtime module fails to type-check for the missing method sealedIdentity and cannot set a field of Identity, and the zero Identity, the only one it can write, gives no Tenant. Mutation check: the test fails when the check it proves is removed or weakened (mutate.py in the builder's notes, 84 mutations, all killed).

title: Only the declared algorithms of the allow list pass, each with its own key type
when: Verifies tokens with alg none, HS256 signed with the public key as the secret, ES256 and PS256, and an RS256 token, with a verifier that names no algorithm; then, with a verifier that names RS256 and ES256 and holds an RSA and a P-256 key, an RS256 and an ES256 token, an ES256 token that names the RSA key, an RS256 token that names the P-256 key, PS256, HS256 and alg none; then an RS256 token with a verifier that names ES256 alone; and calls New with the algorithms none, HS256, PS256, rs256 and RS256 twice.
then: Expects the first four tokens refused and the RS256 token accepted; the RS256 and ES256 tokens of their own keys accepted and every other token refused for its algorithm; the RS256 token refused by the ES256 verifier; and each of those settings refused.
notes: Level: unit. The minter of authn/authntest signs each token. Two alg none tokens: one with no signature, and one over a valid RS256 signature, which only the allow list refuses; HS256 uses the PEM of the RSA public key as the HMAC secret (the algorithm confusion attack). RS256 in lower case is refused too. Mutation check: the test fails when the check it proves is removed or weakened (mutate.py in the builder's notes, 84 mutations, all killed). when: Starts a key set of an issuer of the authntest server and verifies an RS256 token; rotates the key document to a P-256 key after the cooldown and verifies a token of the new key and of the removed key; then starts it with a discovery document of another issuer, of the issuer with a trailing slash, with no issuer, with an http key set URL, a key set URL with a user, no key set URL, the member in other case, a duplicate member, a document that is not JSON, an oversize document, a server failure and a redirect; and starts sources of an http issuer, an issuer with a query, an issuer beside a URL, and an issuer whose server only the CA file trusts.
then: Expects the start to make one discovery request and one key request and the token accepted; after the rotation the new key accepted, the removed key refused, and no second discovery request; each bad document refused at start with an error that names the discovery document and holds no address; the redirect not followed; the three sources refused; and the issuer accepted with the CA file only.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestDiscovery; its subtests carry this ID. With a fake clock for the cooldown. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the key server of authn/authntest serves the discovery document and the key document over TLS on 127.0.0.1 with a test certificate authority, and the test starts and stops it; no hosted identity provider is used. Mutations caught: the issuer member not checked, the jwks_uri not checked for HTTPS, an issuer with a query taken, redirects followed, the CA file not added, the discovery document loaded on each refresh (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc).

title: An ES256 token is verified with a P-256 key of 32-byte coordinates on the curve
when: Verifies an ES256 token of a P-256 key, the same token with a DER signature, with a 63-byte signature and signed by another key; and reads key documents with a point off the curve, a 31-byte x, an x with padding, a key of P-384, a key whose alg is RS256 and a key whose use is enc.
then: Expects the token accepted and the three others refused for the signature, the first three documents refused for the EC key, and the last three keys skipped.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestVerifyES256; its subtest carries this ID. The minter of authn/authntest signs with ES256 as r and s. Mutations caught: the curve not checked, the alg member of an EC key not checked, a point off the curve taken, a signature of another length verified as DER (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc).

title: Settings read each fixed name and refuse a missing setting by its name
when: Reads Settings from an environment with every setting, with each file form in place of its value, and with each required setting left out in turn.
then: Expects each value read from its fixed name or its file, and each missing setting refused with an error that names the setting and holds no value.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestSettings; its subtest carries this ID. The environment is set with t.Setenv, and the value of each setting holds a marker text, so a refusal that shows a value fails the test. The test reads every setting by its value, each file form (DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL_FILE, STEGO_AUTHN_KEYS_FILE), the declared verifier settings, which win, and refuses each required setting left out, a connection file that is missing, a loopback setting that is not 0 or 1 or is set for an address that is not loopback, and a cursor key that is too short. Mutations caught: a declared setting that the environment overrides, a value in a refusal, a short cursor key taken, no key document needed, no TLS to any address.

title: A declaration with discovery takes no key document and the CA file
when: Reads Settings for a declaration that states discovery, two algorithms and the subject claim oid, with STEGO_AUTHN_CA_FILE set and then a declared CA file; and with a key URL, a key file, a declared public key file, a CA file other than the declared one, and a CA file beside a key document file.
then: Expects discovery, the issuer, the algorithms, the subject claim and the CA file in the settings with no key document, the declared CA file to win, and each of the other five refused with an error that names the setting and holds no value.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestSettings; its subtest carries this ID. Mutations caught: a key URL beside discovery taken, an environment CA file that differs from the declared one taken (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc).

title: The key files pass the checks of a connection string file
when: Reads Settings with good key files, then with STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE and then STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE set to a relative path, a missing file, a folder, a FIFO, a link to /dev/zero, a file that group can write, one that other can write, an executable file and a file above 64 KiB; and reads the migration settings with a SpiceDB key file that group can write.
then: Expects the good files read, and each other file refused within 5 s with an error that names the setting and holds no path.
notes: Level: unit. Proved by TestSettingFiles; its subtest carries this ID. Each path holds a secret text, so a refusal that shows the path shows it. Mutations caught: the cursor key and the SpiceDB key read with os.ReadFile, no mode check, a relative path taken (mut/item5.json of b-rt-harden). The second size check, after the read, is not caught alone: the size check of the stat refuses first.

title: New gives the runtimes on pools opened through tenant.Open
when: Calls New with Settings for a local PostgreSQL and a local SpiceDB and the declared parts of a small service, then runs one command and one query through the runtimes it gives.
then: Expects both pools opened through tenant.Open with the verified TLS policy, the command and the query to pass with the tenant set and the decision made, and New refused when SpiceDB cannot be reached.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestNew; its subtest carries this ID. Migrate makes the database first; the test writes the relationships to SpiceDB, calls New, and runs one command, decided on the service-level resource service:todo-svc and written in the tenant t1 under row-level security, and one get query, decided at SpiceDB; a user with no relationship is denied both. Both pools are pools of tenant.Open from the one connection configuration that Parts.TenantConfig gives: the local test gives the adapter's loopback test mode without TLS, so the verified TLS policy itself is the adapter's and is proved under ST-SUP-RP04-LC09. New is refused with an unreachable SpiceDB and with parts that lack a part. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 through pgtest and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image, without privilege, with a preshared key and an in-memory datastore. Mutations caught: no check that SpiceDB answers, one pool for both, no command runtime.

title: Migrate runs the steps in their order on one connection and stops at the first fault
when: Runs Migrate on a fresh database, again on the same database, and on a database where one step fails.
then: Expects the steps in the order of the contract on one connection, the second run to pass, the tenant list owned by the owner role with SELECT and no INSERT for the runtime role and EXECUTE on its provisioning function, the default audit sink table owned by the owner role with SELECT and INSERT and no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE for the worker role and nothing for the runtime role, and the failed run to stop at that step with a fault that names it and no later step run.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestMigrate; its subtest carries this ID. A test hook records the name of each step and the backend of the connection it runs on. Migrate runs on a fresh database and again on the same database, each time in the order of the contract on one connection, with the schema written to SpiceDB twice; the test checks the objects, the grants of the runtime role and the audit partitions. An authorization migration that fails stops the job at authorization_tables with the stage migrate.authorization_tables and no later step, and a foreign table stops it at the ledger check before any write. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 through pgtest and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image, without privilege. Mutations caught: the tables step without the tenant list, two migrations out of order, a step that does not stop the job, a step on a second connection, no grants, the schema written once. The audit sink step runs between the audit step and the idempotency step (ST-SUP-Q98). Mutation caught: the audit sink step with no table (mut/mutate.py of b-q98).

title: Start runs the workers of the selected modes, and Shutdown stops them once
when: Migrates a database, runs a command that updates a row, relates a user to it and stages an effect, then starts the api mode alone, all modes with logins of the worker and relay roles, and a second replica of the controller mode, stops the outbox worker, and shuts the first replica down twice; also reads the worker settings by their names and their file forms.
then: Expects the worker mode refused with no worker role and refused with a bad audit sink setting by its name, the default table given to NewWorker as the audit sink when no sink URL is set, the sink settings read with the worker settings and an http sink URL refused by its name, the api mode alone with no worker, the outbox worker and the relay on their own roles, the effect delivered in its tenant, the relationship written to SpiceDB and its token on the row, the audit row and an anchor of the tenant's chain at the sink, one replica holding the lease, the readiness naming the stopped worker, after Shutdown no component running, the pools closed, the same result for the second call, and the lease taken by the other replica.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestWorkers; its two subtests carry this ID. The test builds the parts as the generated outbox, authorization and audit packages do, with a recording audit sink and a recording destination notify. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 through pgtest and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image, without privilege, with a preshared key and an in-memory datastore. Mutations caught: the outbox worker on the runtime role's pool, a lease name for each holder, the pools left open after Shutdown, no relay, a readiness that ignores a stopped worker, no periodic component, no row of the controller lease. Mutation caught: the sink settings not read with the worker settings (mut/mutate.py of b-q98).

title: The generated service runs its workers through the service runtime
when: Generates the service wiring-shop with stego apply and an after slot on orders bound to a qualified fill, runs only the role migration and a login of each role as the administrator, runs the migration job, which makes the tenant list, starts the binary with all modes and the worker and relay settings, creates an order, sends the command add-note whose Note refers to the order, and adds the tenant to the tenant list.
then: Expects the after slot of the create delivered by the outbox worker as the worker role, the relation note#order written to SpiceDB by the relay so the order's owner may view the note, an anchor boundary of the tenant stored with the anchor in the outbox for the audit sink, one holder of the controller lease, and every mode ready on /readyz/modes.
notes: Level: service. Proved by the subtest of this ID in the check of the generated service, which internal/compiler/runtime_wiring_test.go (TestRuntimeWiring) builds with the pinned Go and runs. The declaration sets the anchor period of audit-log to 2 s. The migration job makes the tenant list (ST-SUP-Q97); the check adds the tenant to it as the administrator, since no Provision command is generated yet (ST-SUP-RC27-G05). The audit-sink messages go to the default table, which ST-SUP-RP14-LC04-T03 checks. The fill order-created of testdata/runtime_wiring/after is qualified with stego test and signed with an SSH key that SIGNERS lists. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 from STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container without privilege, and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image without privilege. Mutations caught: no background task, so the workers never start; no relay in the worker mode; the audit jobs on another tenant list.

title: The generated worker delivers each audit entry and anchor to the default table
when: After the check of ST-SUP-RP14-LC04-T02, with no STEGO_AUDIT_SINK_URL set, waits for the audit-sink messages of the tenant.
then: Expects every audit-sink message of the tenant done, one row of stego_audit_sink.entries for each audit event of the tenant, at least one anchor row, and as many rows as done messages.
notes: Level: service. Proved by the subtest of this ID in the check of the generated service, which internal/compiler/runtime_wiring_test.go (TestRuntimeWiring) builds with the pinned Go and runs. The worker role writes the table through the pool that tenant.Open opened. Before ST-SUP-Q98 was decided, the worker held each message in a sink that refused every delivery, so no message was done and this check fails. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): PostgreSQL 17.7 from STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, a local container without privilege, and a local SpiceDB serve container of the pinned image without privilege. Mutations caught: the held sink given to NewWorker again, the audit sink step left out of the migration job (mut/mutate.py of b-q98). The Product owner decided ST-SUP-Q98 (a) with the default sink on 2026-11-11.

title: The verifier of a declared issuer comes from its discovery document, and a refused start names its stage
when: Calls New with Settings that state discovery through an issuer of the authntest server with its CA file, the algorithm ES256 and the subject claim oid, and verifies an ES256 token and an RS256 token; then calls New when the discovery document names another issuer, and with a key URL that the system roots do not trust.
then: Expects the ES256 token accepted with the subject from oid after one discovery request, the RS256 token refused with no stage, and the stages service.start.authn.discovery and service.start.authn.keys.
notes: Level: integration. Proved by TestNew; its subtest carries this ID. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): the key server of authn/authntest serves the discovery document and the key document over TLS on 127.0.0.1 with a test certificate authority, and the test starts and stops it; no hosted identity provider is used. PostgreSQL comes from pgtest and SpiceDB from a local serve container of the pinned image, as in ST-SUP-RP14-LC02-T01. Mutations caught: New taking the issuer as a key URL, the declared algorithms dropped, the discovery stage named as keys (mut/mutate.py of b-oidc).
